title: The Hussite Field Armies: A Documentary Apparatus, 1420–1434
description:
A documentary apparatus for the Hussite field armies, 1420–1434: how did an army of peasants and townsmen beat five crusades, and why was it destroyed at Lipany? Its thesis: the ordinance won every battle, and the day it was broken, everything was lost. Jan Žižka's military ordinance of 1423 bound lords, townsmen and peasants to one discipline; at Lipany in 1434 the foot left their wagons to pursue a feigned flight and the field armies were destroyed by the lords of Bohemia.

Eight modules from public-domain editions, with the original beside an English translation, every excerpt read against the page images: Žižka's ordinance in Czech (Toman 1898) with Count Lützow's English (1914); the Empire's war orders and wagon orders of 1426–1429 (Toman 1898); Laurence of Březová's Prague chronicle for 1420–1421, the Latin song on the victory at Domažlice (1431) and Bartošek of Drahonice on Malešov and Lipany (all Fontes rerum Bohemicarum V, 1893); Martin V's crusade bull of 1421 (Palacký, Urkundliche Beiträge I, 1873); the Prague Compacts with the Council of Basel, 1433 (Archiv český III, 1844); and Andreas of Regensburg on the raids into Bavaria and Austria and the battle of Hiltersried (Leidinger 1903). Working translations CC0. With a timeline, a Compare page on seventeen questions, nine plates and a list of what is not carried and why.

Continues The Hussite Beginning (1409–1420). Companion game: Řádné poslušenství (https://radne-poslusenstvi.netlify.app/).
